title: The Twist Decomposition of Serial Robots Under Lower-Mobility Tasks
summary: This paper introduces a twist decomposition framework for serial manipulators performing lower mobility tasks. Rather than relying on Jacobian null-space projections, the method separates the end-effector twist into task and redundant components using geometrically defined twist projectors. This formulation provides a direct and intuitive distinction between task-relevant and task-irrelevant motions in operational space, enabling a compact inverse kinematics scheme that naturally handles both manipulator and task redundancy.

AI.tldr: A twist decomposition framework for serial manipulators that separates end-effector motion into task and redundant components using geometric projectors, enabling compact inverse kinematics that handles both manipulator and task redundancy.
AI.motivation: Addresses challenges in performing lower mobility tasks with serial manipulators by moving beyond traditional Jacobian null-space projection approaches.
AI.method: Introduces a twist decomposition framework that separates end-effector twist into task and redundant components using geometrically defined twist projectors instead of Jacobian null-space projections.
AI.result: Provides a direct and intuitive distinction between task-relevant and task-irrelevant motions in operational space, enabling a compact inverse kinematics scheme.
AI.conclusion: The geometrically defined projectors allow the method to naturally handle both manipulator and task redundancy within a compact formulation.

title: Design and stability analysis of an underactuated hand with passively rotating fingers
summary: This paper presents an innovative design and stability analysis of an underactuated robotic finger with spatial mobility, designed to enhance gripping dexterity in robotic hands. The finger architecture incorporates a revolute joint at its base, enabling passive spatial rotation that facilitates both cylindrical and spherical grasping. With only two phalanges per finger, the design simplifies kinematic complexity while supporting precision and enveloping grasps. Stability criteria, based on the moment at the finger base joint induced by contact forces, are introduced to ensure reliable object gripping and prevent ejection during manipulation. The study also examines a differential mechanism that distributes a single actuation torque across multiple fingers, allowing adaptive and coordinated motion. This mechanism enhances the hand's ability to grasp diverse object shapes with minimal pre-grasp adjustments, leveraging passivity for autonomous adaptation. Theoretical findings are experimentally validated using a fully mechanical prototype, demonstrating versatility in performing cylindrical, spherical, parallel, and enveloping grasps. The integration of underactuation-both within individual fingers and among multiple fingers-reduces mechanical complexity, cost, and control demands while preserving functional adaptability. This work advances the development of compliant robotic hands suitable for applications requiring dexterity and robustness, such as agricultural robotics, logistics, assistive technologies, and waste sorting. Future research will focus on automating actuation and refining control strategies to further improve grasp stability and precision, paving the way for autonomous manipulation in unstructured environments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an innovative underactuated robotic finger design with spatial mobility that enhances gripping dexterity through a two-phalange architecture with a base revolute joint, stability criteria based on contact-induced moments, and a differential mechanism for torque distribution across multiple fingers.
AI.motivation: The study aims to develop robotic hands with enhanced gripping dexterity for applications in agricultural robotics, logistics, assistive technologies, and waste sorting. Traditional designs may have excessive complexity, and there is a need for compliant robotic hands that are robust yet require minimal control demands.
AI.method: The research proposes a spatially mobile underactuated finger with two phalanges and a base revolute joint enabling passive spatial rotation. Stability criteria based on the moment at the finger base joint induced by contact forces are derived. A differential mechanism distributes single actuation torque across multiple fingers. Theoretical analysis is experimentally validated using a fully mechanical prototype.
AI.result: Experimental validation demonstrates successful performance of cylindrical, spherical, parallel, and enveloping grasps. The integration of underactuation reduces mechanical complexity, cost, and control requirements while maintaining functional adaptability and the ability to grasp diverse object shapes with minimal pre-grasp adjustments.
AI.conclusion: This work advances compliant robotic hands suitable for dexterity and robustness applications. Future research will focus on automating actuation and refining control strategies to further improve grasp stability and precision for autonomous manipulation in unstructured environments.

title: Bayesian Retraction Optimization for Tissue Attachment Mapping in Surgical Dissection
comment: IEEE IROS 2026 preprint
summary: With growing surgeon shortages, automating surgical sub-tasks such as tissue dissection offers a promising step toward reducing workload and expanding patient access. Prior work has relied on hand-crafted incision policies that cannot quantify uncertainty or has relied on simulation-based methods that require strong modeling assumptions. We instead view tissue attachment identification as an inherently probabilistic problem and propose a Bayesian approach that avoids explicit tissue modeling. Our method uses a Sequential Bayesian Hilbert Map (SBHM) to represent the likelihood that each tissue point is attached to the underlying resection surface. An ensemble of learned classifiers predicts attachment likelihoods from spatial data acquired during robotic tissue retraction, with each classifier serving as a noisy information source to update the SBHM. To plan the next retraction, we devise Bayesian Retraction Optimization (BRO) to select the most informative action under safety constraints. As the SBHM refines over time, regions with high attachment likelihood are selectively incised. We validate our method in simulation across diverse tissue geometries and acquisition strategies, and demonstrate zero-shot transfer to real robotic dissection experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Bayesian approach using Sequential Bayesian Hilbert Map (SBHM) and Bayesian Retraction Optimization (BRO) for automated robotic tissue dissection that quantifies uncertainty and avoids explicit tissue modeling.
AI.motivation: Growing surgeon shortages make automating surgical sub-tasks like tissue dissection valuable. Prior methods either used hand-crafted incision policies that cannot quantify uncertainty or simulation-based methods that require strong modeling assumptions.
AI.method: The method views tissue attachment identification as a probabilistic problem. It uses a Sequential Bayesian Hilbert Map (SBHM) to represent attachment likelihoods of tissue points, an ensemble of learned classifiers as noisy information sources, and Bayesian Retraction Optimization (BRO) to select the most informative action under safety constraints.
AI.result: Validated in simulation across diverse tissue geometries and acquisition strategies, with demonstrated zero-shot transfer to real robotic dissection experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Bayesian framework successfully automates robotic tissue dissection with uncertainty quantification, eliminating the need for explicit tissue modeling assumptions.

title: Agentic Real2Sim: Physics-based World Modeling with Vision-Language Agents
summary: Real-to-sim conversion for robotic interaction with objects remains labor-intensive because it requires more than visual reconstruction: a streamlined real2sim process must recover scene geometries and object states, infer physical parameters, and assemble actors, objects, cameras, poses, and trajectories into a runnable physical simulation. Today this process still depends on manual tuning of visual foundation models, mesh cleanup, coordinate-frame alignment, and brittle workflow glue across visual perception tools and simulators. We introduce \textit{Agentic Real2Sim}, a framework for generalized physical world modeling with vision-language agents, converting a real-world recording of object-robot interaction into a simulatable episodic twin which preserves observations, geometries, robot interactions, and object states. We evaluate Agentic Real2Sim on rigid-object manipulation, deformable-object interaction, and humanoid motion scenes, spanning domains that are usually handled by separate Real2Sim pipelines, marking a first step toward scalable conversion. The framework's agentic decisions can be driven by an open-weight VLM backend at a small fraction of the cost of frontier models, while attaining comparable conversion success rate. We aim to use the resulting real-world-aligned twins for downstream robotics tasks, specifically policy learning and evaluation. The project site is available at https://ericchen321.github.io/agentic_real2sim.github.io/.

AI.tldr: Agentic Real2Sim is a vision-language-agent framework that converts real-world object-robot interaction recordings into simulatable episodic twins preserving observations, geometries, interactions, and states across rigid-object manipulation, deformable-object interaction, and humanoid motion scenes at a fraction of the cost of frontier models.
AI.motivation: Real-to-sim conversion is labor-intensive and requires more than visual reconstruction: it must recover scene geometries, object states, physical parameters, and assemble actors, objects, cameras, poses, and trajectories into a runnable physical simulation. Current processes depend on manual tuning of visual foundation models, mesh cleanup, coordinate-frame alignment, and brittle workflow glue across tools and simulators.
AI.method: A framework using vision-language agents for generalized physical world modeling that converts real-world recordings into simulatable episodic twins while preserving observations, geometries, robot interactions, and object states. The framework's agentic decisions can be driven by an open-weight VLM backend at a small fraction of the cost of frontier models.
AI.result: Evaluated on rigid-object manipulation, deformable-object interaction, and humanoid motion scenes spanning domains that are usually handled by separate Real2Sim pipelines. Achieves comparable conversion success rate to frontier models at a significantly lower computational cost.
AI.conclusion: This marks a first step toward scalable conversion, enabling the use of resulting real-world-aligned twins for downstream robotics tasks such as policy learning and evaluation.

title: Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. Zhongyao Yang and Haoyu Li contributed equally to this work
summary: High-level planning for autonomous driving is a knowledge-intensive engineering decision task that requires accurate scene understanding, timely inference, and internally consistent action selection. Vision-language models (VLMs) can make intermediate reasoning explicit, but their use in deployed planners is constrained by costly structured supervision, unnecessary reasoning in routine scenes, and possible inconsistencies between generated rationales and driving actions. We present a cognitive dual-process planning framework that represents planning-relevant scene knowledge in a machine-parsable structured chain-of-thought (S-CoT) schema. An automated data engine integrates perception foundation models, critical-path filtering, and an expert VLM to generate S-CoT supervision without manual annotation of individual rationales. A lightweight visual Arbiter estimates scene complexity from multilevel vision-encoder features before language decoding and routes each input to either fast meta-action prediction or slow structured reasoning. For slow-path outputs, a deterministic rule-based validator checks whether the parsed S-CoT fields are consistent with the final meta-action and provides verifiable rewards for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). In a 195-scene manual audit, the generated annotations achieve 91.8\% CoT accuracy and a 98.5\% Logical Consistency Score (LCS). On 574 manually verified NAVSIM test samples, the planner achieves 80.14\% planning accuracy and 97.20\% LCS while reducing average latency by 17.39\% relative to applying slow reasoning to every scene. Evaluation on external long-tail subsets further identifies conditions under which routing and planning performance degrade. Together, these results show how explicit scene knowledge can be operationalized through adaptive reasoning and rule-based verification to support high-level VLM planning decisions.

AI.tldr: A cognitive dual-process planning framework for autonomous driving that uses structured chain-of-thought schemas with adaptive reasoning and rule-based verification.
AI.motivation: High-level autonomous driving planning requires accurate scene understanding, timely inference, and internally consistent action selection. VLMs face challenges: costly structured supervision, unnecessary reasoning in routine scenes, and inconsistencies between rationales and driving actions.
AI.method: 1. Represents planning knowledge in machine-parsable structured CoT (S-CoT) schema. 2. Automated data engine (perception foundation models + critical-path filtering + expert VLM) generates S-CoT supervision without manual annotation. 3. Lightweight visual Arbiter estimates scene complexity from vision-encoder features and routes to fast meta-action prediction or slow structured reasoning. 4. Deterministic rule-based validator checks S-CoT consistency with final action and provides verifiable rewards for GRPO.
AI.result: 195-scene audit: 91.8% CoT accuracy, 98.5% Logical Consistency Score (LCS). 574 NAVSIM samples: 80.14% planning accuracy, 97.20% LCS. Average latency reduced by 17.39% vs. applying slow reasoning to all scenes. External long-tail evaluation identifies degradation conditions.
AI.conclusion: Explicit scene knowledge can be operationalized through adaptive reasoning and rule-based verification to support high-level VLM planning decisions in autonomous driving, balancing accuracy, consistency, and efficiency.

title: Computing on the Fly: Navigating a Vision for the Future of Drone Computing
summary:
The report envisions a decade in which drones move goods, medical supplies, and information at a scale comparable to national infrastructure investments like highways and the electric grid. Potential applications include natural disaster detection drones that spot wildfire sources within minutes, medical supply chains that bypass ground congestion to reach rural hospitals, and nationwide fleets that continuously inspect bridges and power lines. Realizing this future, however, requires closing what report authors call a "capability gap," where hardware and aspirations are outpacing the software and systems needed to operate safely at scale.
  The report identifies twelve technical challenges that must be addressed to realize the transformative potential of drone technology: Scaling to millions of drones; AI intelligence and assurance; Edge-cloud continuum and real-time coordination; AI autonomy and agentic systems; Data, training, and validation infrastructure; Critical infrastructure protection; Building reliable fleets from non-deterministic agents; Trust, security, and distributed authentication; Next-generation drone networks; Human-AI partnership and scalable insight; Standards, certification, and regulation; and Workforce development and education.
  These twelve challenges and proposed approaches to them form the basis of the report, laying out a multifaceted path forward for the evolution of done technology.

AI.tldr: This report envisions a future where drones become a critical infrastructure comparable to highways and electric grids, enabling applications like wildfire detection, medical supply chain delivery, and infrastructure inspection. It identifies twelve key technical challenges that must be addressed to close the capability gap between hardware and software systems.
AI.motivation: While drone hardware capabilities have advanced rapidly, the software and systems needed to operate drones safely at scale have not kept pace. This capability gap limits the transformative potential of drone technology despite its promising applications for disaster response, healthcare delivery, and infrastructure monitoring.
AI.method: The authors identified twelve specific technical challenges that must be addressed to realize the full potential of drone technology, including scaling to millions of drones, AI intelligence and assurance, edge-cloud continuum, AI autonomy and agentic systems, data infrastructure, critical infrastructure protection, building reliable fleets from non-deterministic agents, trust and security, next-generation networks, human-AI partnership, standards and regulation, and workforce development.
AI.result: The report presents a comprehensive framework with twelve technical challenges and proposed approaches to each, laying out a multifaceted path forward for the evolution of drone technology.
AI.conclusion: To realize the vision of drones becoming a critical infrastructure comparable to national investments, these twelve technical challenges must be addressed through coordinated efforts in AI, systems engineering, standards development, and workforce training to bridge the capability gap between hardware and software.

title: Eversion-based robots can enable safe access,steering and endoscopic imaging within the spinal subarachnoid space
summary: Safe navigation within the spinal subarachnoid space is constrained by its narrow, compliant, and delicate anatomy. Conventional catheters and continuum robots rely on proximal pushing, generating friction and shear along the tissue device interface that limit distal controllability and increase the risk of neural injury. Here, we present a 2 mm diameter eversion-growing robotic platform that enables friction minimised extension and steering within the human spinal subarachnoid space, validated through computational modelling, phantom experiments, and intact human cadaver studies. The robot integrates a miniature endoscope for real time intrathecal visualisation and advances by pressure driven tip eversion, localising motion to the distal tip while minimising translational sliding of the deployed body. Phantom experiments demonstrated reductions of 65.2% in mean interaction force and 48.0% in peak interaction force compared with matched push-based insertion. Physics based modelling showed that eversion based growth redistributed tissue loading, reducing local stress concentrations and interfacial shear relative to conventional insertion. In an intact human cadaver, the system achieved 150 mm of controlled intrathecal extension with concurrent fluoroscopic and endoscopic visualisation, providing access across multiple vertebral levels from a standard lumbar entry point. Postprocedural laminectomy and durotomy revealed no observable macroscopic disruption of the dura mater or surrounding neural structures. These results provide the first mechanically characterised and multimodally validated demonstration of eversion-based robotic navigation in intact human spinal anatomy, establishing a quantitative and procedural foundation for future intrathecal interventions. Further validation in larger anatomical cohorts and under physiological conditions will be required before clinical translation.

AI.tldr: A 2 mm diameter eversion-growing robotic platform enables friction-minimized extension and steering in the spinal subarachnoid space through pressure-driven tip eversion, validated via computational modeling, phantom experiments, and intact human cadaver studies.
AI.motivation: Safe navigation within the narrow, compliant, and delicate spinal subarachnoid space is constrained by conventional catheters and continuum robots that rely on proximal pushing, generating friction and shear at the tissue-device interface that limit distal controllability and increase neural injury risk.
AI.method: The robot integrates a miniature endoscope for real-time intrathecal visualization and advances via pressure-driven tip eversion, enabling localised motion at the distal tip while minimising translational sliding of the deployed body. Validation was performed through computational modelling, phantom experiments, and intact human cadaver studies.
AI.result: Phantom experiments demonstrated 65.2% reduction in mean interaction force and 48.0% reduction in peak interaction force compared to push-based insertion. Physics-based modeling showed eversion-based growth redistributed tissue loading, reducing local stress concentrations and interfacial shear. In an intact human cadaver, the system achieved 150 mm of controlled intrathecal extension with concurrent fluoroscopic and endoscopic visualization across multiple vertebral levels from a standard lumbar entry point, with no observable macroscopic disruption of dura mater or neural structures.
AI.conclusion: This represents the first mechanically characterised and multimodally validated demonstration of eversion-based robotic navigation in intact human spinal anatomy, establishing a quantitative and procedural foundation for future intrathecal interventions. Further validation in larger anatomical cohorts and physiological conditions is required before clinical translation.

title: Stochastic Multi-Objective Kinodynamic Planning Against Adversaries
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, accepted to CDC 2026
summary: This paper addresses multi-objective kinodynamic planning in environments with stochastic hybrid adversaries that probabilistically transition to adversarial modes based on the ego state. The goal is to construct the Pareto-front of paths that trade off execution cost and the probability of safety constraint violation (risk). Existing chance-constrained planners evaluate risk over open-loop trajectories, yielding overly conservative solutions that fail to account for ego-agent reactivity. To address this limitation, we shift the planning space to sequences of closed-loop policies, and integrate sample-based risk evaluation directly into tree construction via Monte-Carlo particle rollouts. We first introduce Stochastic Multi-Objective RRT (SMO-RRT), for which we prove probabilistic completeness, followed by Stochastic Multi-Objective Stable Sparse RRT (SMO-SST), which leverages selective pruning to improve numerical performance at the cost of completeness. For both algorithms, we derive a finite-sample bound on the probability of chance constraint violation for systems with non-Gaussian, state-dependent uncertainty, enabling probabilistically safe planning in a broad class of environments applicable to multi-agent systems, social navigation, and autonomous driving.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces two sampling-based algorithms (SMO-RRT and SMO-SST) for multi-objective kinodynamic planning that evaluate risk over closed-loop trajectories using Monte-Carlo particle rollouts, enabling safe planning with stochastic hybrid adversaries in multi-agent systems and autonomous driving applications.
AI.motivation: Existing chance-constrained planners evaluate risk over open-loop trajectories, yielding overly conservative solutions that fail to account for ego-agent reactivity. The authors seek to address this limitation by shifting the planning space to sequences of closed-loop policies and integrating sample-based risk evaluation directly into tree construction.
AI.method: The authors introduce Stochastic Multi-Objective RRT (SMO-RRT), which is probabilistically complete, and Stochastic Multi-Objective Stable Sparse RRT (SMO-SST), which leverages selective pruning for improved numerical performance. Both algorithms integrate Monte-Carlo particle rollouts into tree construction to evaluate risk over closed-loop trajectories. A key contribution is deriving a finite-sample bound on the probability of chance constraint violation for systems with non-Gaussian, state-dependent uncertainty.
AI.result: Both SMO-RRT and SMO-SST enable probabilistically safe planning in environments with stochastic hybrid adversaries. The derived finite-sample bound allows for planning with non-Gaussian, state-dependent uncertainty. These algorithms are applicable to multi-agent systems, social navigation, and autonomous driving scenarios.
AI.conclusion: By shifting from open-loop to closed-loop trajectory evaluation and providing theoretical guarantees through finite-sample bounds, the proposed algorithms overcome the conservatism of existing chance-constrained planners while maintaining probabilistic safety. This enables more efficient and practical solutions for real-world applications requiring trade-offs between execution cost and safety risk.

title: From Distances to Trajectories: Real-Time Signed Distance Function Mapping and Distance-Accelerated Motion Planning for UAVs
comment: 25 pages, 10 figures, 5 tables
summary: Autonomous flight in cluttered environments requires a robot to build a geometric map of its surroundings and plan safe, dynamically feasible trajectories, all onboard and in real time. Conventional approaches treat mapping and planning as separate stages and often rely on binary occupancy for collision checking. We argue that these two stages should be co-designed around a single representation: a signed distance function (SDF). By encoding distance to the nearest obstacle, an SDF provides richer information for planning and trajectory optimization than occupancy alone. We develop an Octree REsidual Network (OREN) that pairs an explicit octree prior with an implicit neural residual to reconstruct SDFs online from point cloud observations with the efficiency of volumetric methods and the accuracy and differentiability of neural methods. In tandem, we develop Bubble$^\star$, a search-based planner that exploits the distance information to grow maximal collision-free balls, which we call bubbles, with formal guarantees of termination, completeness, and failure detection. Planning over a graph of bubbles significantly reduces collision checks compared to a grid-based A$^\star$ search and returns a bubble sequence that forms a safe corridor for trajectory optimization. We demonstrate the integrated OREN-Bubble$^\star$ approach onboard a quadrotor, navigating unseen indoor environments in real time under tight compute constraints. OREN improves SDF estimation by $22$% compared to baselines, while Bubble$^\star$ finds trajectories spanning $\approx 90$ m through a cluttered environment in $1$-$3$ sec., whereas baselines take up to $10$ sec. in the same environment.

AI.tldr: A co-designed system for autonomous flight that uses signed distance functions (SDFs) for both mapping and planning, combining an Octree REsidual Network (OREN) for SDF reconstruction with a Bubble$^\star$ planner that grows collision-free bubbles to generate safe trajectories.
AI.motivation: Conventional approaches treat mapping and planning as separate stages using binary occupancy for collision checking, which lacks sufficient information for planning and trajectory optimization. The authors argue these stages should be co-designed around a single representation (SDF) that encodes distance to obstacles.
AI.method: Two key components: (1) OREN (Octree REsidual Network) - combines explicit octree prior with implicit neural residual to reconstruct SDFs online from point clouds, (2) Bubble$^\star$ - a search-based planner that grows maximal collision-free balls ("bubbles") using distance information from SDFs, forming a safe corridor for trajectory optimization.
AI.result: OREN improves SDF estimation by 22% compared to baselines. Bubble$^\star$ finds trajectories spanning ~90 m through cluttered environments in 1-3 seconds, whereas baselines take up to 10 seconds. The system successfully navigates unseen indoor environments onboard a quadrotor in real time under tight compute constraints.
AI.conclusion: The integrated OREN-Bubble$^\star$ approach demonstrates that co-designing mapping and planning around SDFs enables efficient, real-time autonomous flight in cluttered environments, providing superior performance compared to conventional separate-stage approaches.
